checks.title: Canonical (Sleeper) keys
checks.summary: 39 rules. 1:1 Sleeper key: 32 (split by player/team defense: 101 KRTD, 102 PRTD). Exact via several Sleeper keys: 1 — 80 FG0 (0–39 = fgm_0_19 + fgm_20_29 + fgm_30_39). Need a derived rule: 4 — 92 PA14 (ESPN 14–17 vs Sleeper pts_allow_14_20: no exact cover); 122 PA22 (ESPN 22–27 vs Sleeper pts_allow_21_27: no exact cover); 124 PA35 (ESPN 35–45 vs Sleeper pts_allow_35p: no exact cover); 125 PA46 (ESPN 46+ vs Sleeper pts_allow_35p: no exact cover). No Sleeper key: 2 — 93 BLKKRTD (no dedicated Sleeper key (def_st_td may include blocked-kick return TDs; unverified)); 209 1PSF ("1pt Safety"). Shared Sleeper keys: def_td ← 103, 104 (equal points, one rate works). Candidate keys Sleeper didn't return in Phase 0: none. Completed week(s) 2 and 3: 14 of 24 rostered D/ST lines had points allowed where ESPN's bucket (0, 1–6, 7–13, 14–17, 18–21, 22–27, 28–34, 35–45, 46+) differs from Sleeper's (0, 1–6, 7–13, 14–20, 21–27, 28–34, 35+): 4.2% of the 331 player-weeks in the oracle. Raw points allowed (stat 120 PTSA → Sleeper pts_allow) is on 24/24 of those lines, so a derived rule is computable. Ranges are computed from espn-api labels and Sleeper key names; the other candidates are judgement (scripts/lib/espn/canonical.ts) until the Phase 1 oracle recomputes ESPN's points through Sleeper keys.

decisions: ID tables and X-Fantasy-Filter payloads are taken from cwendt94/espn-api@663d726 (MIT): constant.py is parsed at run time (scripts/lib/espn/constants.ts), filters are copied verbatim with a drift check (scripts/lib/espn/filters.ts); upstream behaviour the report cites is checked against the fetched source files.

Position = espn-api's eligibleSlots rule; the defaultPositionId table is derived empirically from the active player universe (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 4 TE, 5 K, 7 P, 9 DT, 10 DE, 11 LB, 12 CB, 13 S, 14 HC, 15 TQB, 16 D/ST) and cross-checked against Sleeper's and DynastyProcess's espn_id → position (E.defaultPosition).

pointsOverrides are keyed by the player's defaultPositionId and REPLACE the base points (key space: 5/5 discriminating player-weeks; replace vs add: 72/72; K.overrideKeys), which matches the spec's byPosition rule once keys are translated to positions. Keys for positions without a discriminating player-week (e.g. QB, K) are inferred.

League type: keeperCount 0 → redraft (settled for Parker's league: redraft); keeperCount ≥ active roster → dynasty, otherwise keeper: that part is inferred and untested (no ESPN keeper/dynasty league probed; ESPN has no dynasty flag).

Transactions: request scoringPeriodId 1…current with espn-api's type filter and dedupe rows by id across requests. scoringPeriodId 0 returns the current period's rows (G.periodZero) and so does the next period (G.periodAhead), so only 1…current are requested. Lineup moves (ROSTER) are excluded. Phase 1's activity feature counts unique ids.

Free agents: one request per position with espn-api's free_agents() filter at limit 500 (espn-api's pool page size), then ranked by projection for the top 50 (H.top50). Future-week projections: espn-api's pool filter, page of 500, sampled weeks only, cached 6 h (§2.10).

Canonical scoring keys: range rules (points/yards allowed, FG distance, 100-199 yard games) are mapped by computing ranges from espn-api labels vs Sleeper key names; other rules use a candidate table (scripts/lib/espn/canonical.ts) that the Phase 1 oracle must confirm (C.canonical).

Sanitized fixtures drop members[].notificationSettings, player analyst text/rankings (seasonOutlook, outlooks, rankings, draftRanksByRankType), creationInfo/lastUpdateInfo.platform and clientAddress (which app a member used) and previous seasons' stat lines; per-week fixtures keep only that week's lines; free-agent fixtures keep the 50 most-owned plus the top 50 by projection; raw captures keep everything. Team/member/division name fields are replaced by path; purely numeric names are never registered with the text scrubber (it would rewrite that number everywhere in report text).

The public test league's id is not registered in the redaction map (CLAUDE.md itself contains it, so check:leaks would flag the spec); its fixtures replace it with the fixed placeholder 100002 and URLs use {publicLeagueId}.
Parker's own first name stays readable in reports ("Parker's team"); his member record is masked in fixtures (Owner/First/Last + his team id) like everyone else's.

Injury mapping proposal: ACTIVE→ACTIVE, QUESTIONABLE→QUESTIONABLE, DOUBTFUL→DOUBTFUL, OUT→OUT, INJURY_RESERVE→IR, SUSPENSION→SUSPENDED, DAY_TO_DAY and PROBABLE→QUESTIONABLE, missing (team D/ST)→ACTIVE; injuryReturnWeek from kona_playercard injuryDetails.expectedReturnDate (E.injuryReturn).

Trade history for the acceptance model: read TRADE_* rows per scoring period (proposals list their legs); if TRADE_ACCEPT rows arrive without items, refill them from player cards (players[].transactions) as espn-api does, or from recent-activity messages (TRADED).
